meta.title: Microblog Platform
meta.summary: A reference demo plan for the Microblog platform — a multi-tenant microblog with real-time fan-out timelines, threaded conversations, media uploads, full-text search, and notifications.
meta.userIdea: A Twitter-like social platform where people share short posts (up to 280 characters), reply in threads, like and repost, attach images or short videos, follow other users, and get a real-time personal feed of updates from people they follow. Includes public search and trending topics, private direct messages, multiple separate communities, and basic moderation tools. For creative ppl

systemOverview.purpose: Deliver a fast, accessible microblog platform with real-time fan-out timelines, threaded conversations, media uploads, search, and direct messages.
systemOverview.context: Replaces a legacy single-server blog with a distributed microblog: a Python FastAPI backend, dedicated fan-out workers, an Angular SPA, and a managed Postgres plus Redis plus OpenSearch stack.
constraints: Public timelines must render in under 2 seconds on 4G.
Fan-out latency p95 under 1 second from publish to follower timeline.
Direct messages must be encrypted at rest with envelope encryption.
nfrs: p95 home feed render under 1.5s on a warm cache.
WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for all public pages.
Zero PII in logs; structured logging with correlation IDs.

boundedContexts.name: Identity and Access
boundedContexts.description: Manages user accounts, OAuth and OIDC logins, sessions, and the verification badge.

ubiquitousLanguage.UserAccount: A registered user with a unique handle, a display name, and a verification state.
ubiquitousLanguage.Session: A server-side record of an authenticated client bound to a refresh token id.
ubiquitousLanguage.VerificationBadge: A per-user indicator of trust granted by the verification-badge domain service.

boundedContexts.name: Social Graph
boundedContexts.description: Tracks follow, block, and mute relationships between users.

ubiquitousLanguage.FollowEdge: A directed edge from follower to followee, with a creation timestamp.
ubiquitousLanguage.BlockList: A per-user list of blocked accounts; blocks suppress interactions both ways.
ubiquitousLanguage.MuteList: A per-user list of muted accounts; mutes hide posts but preserve follows.

boundedContexts.name: Posts and Threads
boundedContexts.description: Owns the post, thread, and media-attachment aggregates and their read APIs.

ubiquitousLanguage.Post: A short post with up to 280 characters and a lifecycle status.
ubiquitousLanguage.Thread: An ordered self-reply chain anchored on a root post.
ubiquitousLanguage.MediaAttachment: A reference from a post to one or more media variants owned by the media context.

boundedContexts.name: Engagement
boundedContexts.description: Records likes, reposts, and bookmarks per user-post pair.

ubiquitousLanguage.Like: A user-post pair indicating a positive engagement.
ubiquitousLanguage.Repost: A user-post pair indicating a repost; plain or quote.
ubiquitousLanguage.Bookmark: A private per-user pointer to a post, ordered by recency.

boundedContexts.name: Media
boundedContexts.description: Owns media uploads, variants, and the transcoding worker.

ubiquitousLanguage.MediaUpload: A single upload tracked from request through ready variants.
ubiquitousLanguage.MediaVariant: A single transcoded rendition (thumbnail, medium, full, HLS).
ubiquitousLanguage.MediaProcessor: A service that turns a raw upload into ready variants.

boundedContexts.name: Search and Trending
boundedContexts.description: Indexes published posts into OpenSearch and computes trending topics.

ubiquitousLanguage.SearchIndex: The OpenSearch index of published posts with typeahead and full-text search.
ubiquitousLanguage.TrendingItem: A ranked hashtag or topic over a rolling 24-hour window with half-life decay.
ubiquitousLanguage.IndexingQueue: An in-memory buffer that batches index events to OpenSearch.

boundedContexts.name: Notifications
boundedContexts.description: Creates and dispatches in-app notifications with coalescing and push fan-out.

ubiquitousLanguage.Notification: A per-user record describing a like, repost, mention, follow, or DM event.
ubiquitousLanguage.Mention: A handle reference extracted from a post or DM body for notification purposes.
ubiquitousLanguage.FanoutScheduler: A coalescing dispatcher that decides when to push a notification.

boundedContexts.name: Direct Messaging
boundedContexts.description: Owns 1:1 private DM threads, message delivery, and read-state tracking.

ubiquitousLanguage.DMConversation: A 1:1 conversation between two users with ordered messages.
ubiquitousLanguage.DMMessage: A private text or media message with send and read state.
ubiquitousLanguage.DeliveryReceipt: A per-recipient pointer to the last delivered message.

boundedContexts.name: Communities
boundedContexts.description: Owns user-created communities, membership roles, and scoped timelines.

ubiquitousLanguage.Community: A named group with members, posts, and moderators.
ubiquitousLanguage.CommunityMembership: A user-to-community edge with owner, mod, or member role.
ubiquitousLanguage.CommunityPost: A post whose visibility is scoped to a single community.

boundedContexts.name: Moderation
boundedContexts.description: Owns content reports, automated policy checks, and action ledgers.

ubiquitousLanguage.ContentReport: A user-submitted report against a post, DM, or account.
ubiquitousLanguage.ModerationAction: A logged decision by an automated rule or moderator.
ubiquitousLanguage.PolicyRule: A rule that emits ModerationActions when matched.

boundedContexts.name: Feed and Timeline
boundedContexts.description: Aggregates the home timeline from posts, reposts, and follows with scoring.

ubiquitousLanguage.HomeTimeline: A materialized feed of recent posts from followed users.
ubiquitousLanguage.FeedItem: A scored timeline entry: post, repost, or reply.
ubiquitousLanguage.TimelineFanout: The merge of post events into follower timelines.

architectureLayers.summary: FastAPI service that owns the publish, reply, engagement, and social-graph bounded contexts behind REST and WebSocket APIs. Follows Clean Architecture (domain, application, infrastructure, interfaces) with DDD aggregates per context, an outbox table for reliable domain events, and ARQ workers that fan out timelines and notifications.

technicalContext.storage: PostgreSQL 16 via SQLAlchemy 2 async; Redis 7 for hot caches and timeline fan-out; S3-compatible object storage for media; OpenSearch 2 for search and trending
technicalContext.targetPlatform: Linux server (Python 3.11) containerised via Docker; deployed behind a reverse proxy with TLS termination
technicalContext.performanceGoals: p95 GET home timeline under 200ms; p95 POST post under 400ms; fan-out worker sustains 50k posts per minute at peak
technicalContext.constraints: Domain layer MUST have zero framework imports; every status transition MUST be idempotent and emit exactly one domain event via the outbox; all authorization checks MUST live in the application layer, never in routes
technicalContext.scaleScope: 1M MAU readers, 50k posts per minute at peak, 200 RPS on read endpoints, 50 RPS on write endpoints

constitutionCheck: Strict type checking on every Pydantic schema (extra=forbid) and mypy --strict on the application layer
At least 2 unit tests plus 1 integration test per use case, with the domain layer tested without I/O
Domain layer has zero framework imports (no FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Redis, boto3, or OpenSearch client)
Outbox pattern is used for every domain event; no synchronous cross-context calls from request handlers
All authorization checks live in the application layer; routes never short-circuit policy decisions
Background work runs only in ARQ workers; the web process never executes long jobs inline

architectureLayers.summary: ARQ-based worker processes for fan-out, notifications, search indexing, media transcoding, and DM delivery. Each worker consumes a single Redis stream, deduplicates by event id, and writes back to PostgreSQL, Redis, S3, OpenSearch, or the realtime push gateway. Workers expose a /healthz endpoint and emit OpenTelemetry spans per event.

technicalContext.storage: Redis Streams for input; PostgreSQL, S3, and OpenSearch for output
technicalContext.performanceGoals: Fan-out dispatcher processes 10k events per minute per replica with p95 latency under 1s
technicalContext.constraints: Workers must be idempotent on event id; transient errors retry with exponential backoff up to 5 times
technicalContext.scaleScope: 1k concurrent jobs per replica across 6 worker kinds, 3 replicas each

constitutionCheck: Every worker job is idempotent on its event id
Workers never call the API directly; they consume events from Redis Streams
Every job emits an OpenTelemetry span with the event id as an attribute
Failed jobs go to a per-stream DLQ after 5 retries
Worker processes expose a /healthz endpoint

domains.name: Identity and Access
domains.description: Manages user identity lifecycle, authentication credentials, profile attributes, and account state for the microblog platform. Acts as the trusted source of identity used by every other bounded context.
responsibilities: Register new user accounts with unique username, email, and hashed credentials
Authenticate users via password verification and issue short-lived access tokens
Maintain and validate user profile attributes such as display name, bio, and avatar URL
Handle account verification, password reset requests, and account deactivation flows
Expose a stable repository contract so other bounded contexts can look up users by id or handle

aggregates.name: UserAccount
aggregates.description: The aggregate root representing a registered member of the platform. It owns credentials, profile attributes, and lifecycle status, and enforces the consistency rules that keep the identity context self-contained.
invariants: Username must be unique across the platform and match ^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$
Email address must be unique and syntactically valid
Password is never stored in plaintext; only its hash is persisted
A deactivated account cannot authenticate, reactivate, or update its profile

domainEvents.name: UserRegistered
domainEvents.description: Published when a new account successfully completes registration.

domainEvents.name: UserAuthenticated
domainEvents.description: Published after a successful password-based login. Carries no credentials.

domainEvents.name: ProfileUpdated
domainEvents.description: Published when a user changes any profile-level attribute such as name, bio, or avatar.

domainEvents.name: PasswordResetRequested
domainEvents.description: Published when a user requests a password reset, signalling the notifications context to send a reset link.

components.name: UserAccount Aggregate
components.description: Domain aggregate root for registered users; encapsulates identity, credentials, profile, and lifecycle invariants.
responsibilities: Enforce uniqueness and format rules for username and email
Expose commands that mutate account state and emit corresponding events
Refuse commands that violate aggregate invariants
components.errorHandling: Invariants throw typed DomainError subclasses; never throw generic Error; failed commands return the aggregate to its prior state.
acceptanceCriteria: Registering with a duplicate username is rejected with UsernameAlreadyTaken
Registering with a duplicate email is rejected with EmailAlreadyRegistered
Storing a user persists only the hash, never the plaintext password
Deactivated accounts throw on every mutating command
All state-changing commands emit exactly one domain event

then: the aggregate stores a PasswordHash, not the plaintext

components.name: Authentication Service
components.description: Domain service that verifies passwords against stored hashes and mints short-lived bearer tokens for use across the platform.
responsibilities: Compare a presented password to the stored hash using constant-time comparison
Issue a signed bearer token carrying the userId and sessionId
Reject authentication for deactivated accounts
components.errorHandling: Failures return typed errors (InvalidCredentials, AccountInactive, TokenInvalid) rather than throwing generic exceptions; never leak whether the username exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Authentication with the correct password returns a signed token whose payload contains userId
Authentication with the wrong password returns InvalidCredentials and reveals no account existence
Deactivated accounts always fail authentication regardless of password correctness
Tokens have an expiry no longer than 15 minutes and are verifiable by verifyToken
verifyToken rejects tokens signed with a different secret or past their expiry

given: a token issued by a different signer instance

components.name: UserAccount Repository
components.description: Persistence port and adapter for UserAccount aggregates, exposing lookups by id, username, and email.
responsibilities: Persist and rehydrate UserAccount aggregates transactionally
Enforce unique indexes on username and email at the storage layer

articles.title: Library-First
articles.content: Each bounded context ships as a standalone library with a public API and a CLI surface, owned by exactly one team.

articles.title: CLI Interface
articles.content: Every library exposes a CLI entry point for ad-hoc operations and integration testing; the CLI is the canonical operator interface.

articles.title: Test-First (TDD)
articles.content: Tests are written before implementation. Every component ships with a tddSpec that lists BDD Given/When/Then scenarios covering the happy path and the primary failure mode.

articles.title: Integration Testing
articles.content: Real dependencies are exercised in integration tests; only repositories and external adapters are stubbed.

articles.title: Observability
articles.content: Structured logs with correlation IDs, OpenTelemetry traces, and Prometheus metrics at every cross-process boundary.

articles.title: Versioning & Breaking Changes
articles.content: Breaking changes require a major version bump and a migration note. Wire payloads use a `.vN` suffix; consumer is responsible for handling at least N-1.

articles.title: Simplicity
articles.content: Prefer the simplest solution that satisfies the constitution checks. Reject premature abstractions and premature optimisation.

articles.title: Anti-Abstraction
articles.content: No interface or base class without at least two concrete consumers in the current plan. Repositories do not exist before a second implementation appears.

articles.title: Integration-First Delivery
articles.content: Every change ships with at least one integration test that exercises the new path end-to-end. Pure unit-test additions are not a release blocker on their own.

workflows.name: Publish and Fan-out
workflows.description: Author publishes a post; the fan-out worker materialises the post into follower timelines and indexes it for search.
steps: Author opens the composer and clicks Post.
POST /api/posts persists the post and writes an outbox event in the same transaction.
PubSub bus publishes post.published.v1 to the fan-out and search streams.
Fan-out dispatcher loads followers and writes per-user timeline rows in 500-row batches.
Timeline cache prepends the new post id to each follower cache and trims to 800 entries.
SPA home feed receives the new post on the next refresh or pull-to-refresh.

workflows.name: Engage and Notify
workflows.description: A like, reply, repost, or mention triggers an in-app notification and updates engagement counters atomically.
steps: Reader likes a post from the home feed or thread view.
POST /api/likes persists the like and writes engagement.recorded.v1.
Reply or repost persists the new post and emits reply.created.v1 or repost.created.v1.
Notification worker detects engagement events and creates a Notification aggregate.
Fan-out scheduler coalesces notifications and dispatches WSS push to the recipient.
The author sees the notification in the panel within 2 seconds.

workflows.name: Upload and Process
workflows.description: Author attaches media (image or short video) to a post; the media worker produces CDN-served variants.
steps: Author attaches an image or short video in the composer.
Backend issues a presigned URL and records the upload in pending status.
Client uploads directly to the presigned URL and calls markUploaded.
Media worker transcodes into thumbnail, medium, and full variants.
Variants are uploaded to the object store and CDN URLs are returned.
The post publish flow attaches variants and emits post.published.v1.

workflows.name: Search and Trend
workflows.description: Search indexer ingests published posts; the trending calculator updates the explore page with half-life decay.
steps: Fan-out emits post.published.v1 and post.deleted.v1 to the search indexer stream.
Indexing queue buffers posts up to 500 items or 2 seconds.
Indexing queue flushes a bulk request to OpenSearch and retries with backoff on failure.
Trending calculator applies half-life decay to recent engagements per hashtag.
Explore page serves the top-N trending hashtags from the 60-second snapshot.

workflows.name: Report and Enforce
workflows.description: Reader reports a post; a staff moderator triages and applies an enforcement action via the BlockList.
steps: Reader clicks Report on a post and submits a form with a reason.
POST /api/reports persists the report and emits report.created.v1.
Triage service assigns the report to the least-loaded moderator with capacity.
Staff reviews the report and applies an enforcement action via the BlockList (hide, soft-delete, suspend).
Backend persists the block and emits graph.blocked.v1 or post.hidden.v1.
The reported post is hidden from the reporter's timelines within 5 seconds.

workflows.name: Join and Participate in a Community
workflows.description: User discovers a community, joins, and posts within it; community-scoped fan-out keeps timelines separated.
steps: Visitor browses the Communities directory and opens a community page.
Signed-in user clicks Join; membership is persisted and community.joined.v1 is emitted.
User opens the community composer; body and media are validated against community rules.
POST /api/posts with communityId persists the post scoped to the community.
Fan-out writes the post to community-member timelines only, not the global home feed.
Community moderators can pin or remove posts via the moderation tool.

adrs.title: Fan-out on write for home timelines
adrs.context: Home timelines must render in under 200ms p95 from a warm cache. Fan-out on read would force a join over follow edges on every read.
adrs.decision: Use fan-out on write via a Redis stream and a dedicated worker that materialises per-user timeline rows and caches.
consequences: Hot authors (verified accounts) require sharded workers to keep up.
Unfollow requires dematerialisation; dematerialisation is implemented by the worker on graph.unfollowed.v1.
Read latency drops from multi-second joins to sub-50ms cache reads.
Community posts fan out only to community members, keeping global home feed size bounded.

adrs.title: PostgreSQL plus Redis for the primary store
adrs.context: We need strong consistency for posts, follows, and engagement with sub-millisecond read latency for hot timelines.
adrs.decision: Use PostgreSQL 16 as the system of record and Redis 7 for the hot-path timeline cache and Redis Streams.
consequences: Postgres handles transactional outbox writes for fan-out reliability.
Redis is treated as a cache; a cold cache falls back to Postgres reads.
Redis failover can lose up to 5 seconds of cache writes; reads recover from Postgres.

adrs.title: OpenSearch for full-text and trending
adrs.context: Typeahead and full-text search must return results in under 100ms p95 across tens of millions of posts.
adrs.decision: Index published posts into OpenSearch with a dedicated indexer worker and a buffered bulk request strategy.
consequences: A deleted post is removed from the index within 5 seconds.
Trending snapshots are recomputed from the index with a 60-second TTL.
Index failures fall back to a Postgres full-text search query path.

adrs.title: S3-compatible object storage plus CDN for media
adrs.context: Media uploads include images up to 50MB and videos up to 500MB and must be served with low latency worldwide.
adrs.decision: Store raw and transcoded media in S3-compatible object storage and serve variants through a CDN.
consequences: Presigned URLs keep uploads off the API server.
Variant generation is idempotent on upload id.
CDN cache invalidation is required when a media variant is moderated.

adrs.title: NgRx signalStore for frontend state
adrs.context: We need fast, signal-based state management with a clear audit boundary between reads and writes.
adrs.decision: Standalone Angular components only, NgRx signalStore for feature state, mutate only via patchState inside withMethods.
consequences: Components cannot mutate state directly; they call store methods.
Schema validation runs at the API service boundary before reaching stores.
Smaller bundles and clearer feature ownership.

adrs.title: Zod schemas shared between frontend and backend
adrs.context: Type drift between the Angular SPA and the FastAPI backend has caused production schema_drift errors.
adrs.decision: Write every API contract once in Zod (frontend) and mirror it in Pydantic (backend); generate TypeScript types via z.infer and OpenAPI from Zod.
consequences: No hand-written TypeScript request or response types.
Schema changes require a codegen run on CI; CI fails on uncommitted generated artefacts.
Breaking changes require a new .vN suffix on the event name.
